video_caption: The video segment opens with a young man, dressed in a dark, possibly plaid shirt, peering intently from beneath a wooden shelf, seemingly browsing books. This transitions to a bearded man with glasses, wearing a plaid shirt, holding his head in frustration against a blackboard filled with intricate mathematical and chemical equations. Next, a close-up shows light-skinned hands rapidly flipping through the pages of a large, dark book. The scene then changes to a black and white image of an ancient Sumerian cylinder seal, depicting three figures and celestial symbols, with the text "The Sumerian Seal, Flickr/Tortuga767" visible at the top. Finally, the segment displays four ancient rectangular clay tablets, covered in cuneiform script, with "Enuma Elish" written in the top left corner.

The video opens with a static shot of four ancient cuneiform tablets, appearing to be made of clay and covered in dense Akkadian cuneiform script. The text "Enuma Elish" is displayed in the upper left corner. At 0:13, the scene transitions to a black and white diagram titled "Fig. 111," depicting a simplified solar system. Concentric circles represent "ORBITS OF PLANETS" around the "SUN" and "EARTH'S ORBIT," while a large, highly elliptical orbit labeled "ORBIT OF 12th PLANET" stretches far out to a point marked "APOGEE." Below the diagram, the text "Nibiru 12th Planet Orbital Period: 3600 years" is displayed. At 0:20, the visual changes to a screenshot of a webpage titled "Caltech Researchers Find Evidence of a Real Ninth Planet," dated "January 20, 2016." The article describes "Planet Nine," a giant planet with a highly elongated orbit in the outer solar system. A red bracket highlights a sentence stating, "In fact, it would take this new planet between 10,000 and 20,000 years to make just one full orbit around the sun." To the right of the article text, a dark, spherical planet is visible in an artistic rendering.

The video segment opens at 00:03 with a cosmic scene against a dark background filled with numerous stars of varying sizes and colors, predominantly blueish-white and some orange. In the top-left corner, white text reads "T-Tauri Star." A faint, golden U-shaped object is visible in the center, while a very bright, white, star-like object with prominent diffraction spikes (a cross shape) is located in the bottom-right. At 00:04, the scene transitions to an animated diagram of a solar system against a starry background. A large yellow sun is at the center, surrounded by nine concentric elliptical orbits representing the planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth (green), Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto, each labeled with their names and depicted as small colored circles. Below these orbits, the white text "Orbit of the Planets" is displayed. A much larger, highly elliptical orbit, outlined in red with red dashed lines, encompasses the entire solar system diagram. A small red circle labeled "Nibiru" in red text is positioned at the outermost point of this red elliptical orbit, far from the central sun. In the top-left corner, the website address "conhecimentohj.com" (knowledge today.com) is visible, and a small, cartoon-like depiction of a man's head is in the top-right corner.

The video begins with a wide shot of a dark blue, cloudy cosmic background filled with numerous, irregularly shaped dark grey asteroids or rocks of varying sizes, seemingly floating in space, with small white dots resembling stars scattered throughout. This scene transitions at 0:14 to a black background featuring a large, light blue/grey planet, identified as Uranus, encircled by several thin, bright rings. The planet exhibits a vibrant greenish-blue aurora-like glow on its left side and three small, distinct red dots on its right hemisphere. In the top left corner, white text reads "NASA/Erich Karkoschka (Univ. Arizona)", indicating the source of the image. A very small, dark, and indistinct image of a person's head and shoulders is visible in the top right corner.

The video opens with a screenshot of a webpage featuring the title "What Are the Causes of Perturbations the Orbit of Planet Uranus?" (English). The webpage header includes "SCIENCING" and navigation links like "SCIENCE," "MATH," "PROJECTS," and "NEWS," with "Home > Science > Physics > Astronomy" displayed below the main logo. A small profile picture, possibly of Isaac Newton, is visible in the top right. The central image on the page depicts a light blue planet with thin rings, set against a starry cosmic background. This static image then transitions to an animated depiction of a similar blue-green planet with more vibrant, yellowish rings against a dark blue, star-filled space background with subtle nebulae. Two smaller, reddish-orange planetary bodies are also visible on either side of the main planet, and the text "Stocktrek Images" (English) appears in the top left corner. Throughout this visual, a male narrator discusses the "unusual signs of an unsteady orbit" and a "wobble" of Uranus, attributing it to "something incredibly dense."

The video segment opens with a black and white portrait of an elderly man identified as P.A. Hansen, featuring a long white beard, wild white hair, and glasses, wearing a dark jacket and white shirt. This transitions to a black and white engraving depicting Jean-Joseph Le Verrier explaining the discovery of Neptune to French King Louis Philippe, with Le Verrier, a man with dark curly hair, holding papers while speaking to the King, who has lighter wavy hair and is gesturing, all set against a backdrop of an armillary sphere and shelves. Following this, an oval-framed black and white portrait of Jacques Babinet appears, showing a man with gray hair and a serious expression, adorned with a medal on his formal attire. The video then switches to an animated representation of the solar system on a black background, where multiple colored dots, representing planets including Mercury (orange), Venus (pink), Earth (light blue), Mars (dark blue), Saturn (light brown with a ring), and Uranus (darker blue), orbit a central yellow dot (the Sun), illustrating their paths as the camera slightly zooms out and pans, with the animation credited to Riccardo Di Sipio. Throughout all these scenes, a small, dark portrait of a man remains in the top right corner.

The video displays a large, pale blue-grey celestial body, likely a gas or ice giant planet, filling most of the frame from the bottom left to the top right. Its surface shows subtle, swirling patterns of lighter and darker blue-grey, suggesting atmospheric features or cloud bands. In the top left corner, white text reads "Voyager 2," indicating the source of the image. In the top right corner, a small, square, sepia-toned image depicts a historical portrait of a man, possibly a scientist or astronomer, with dark hair and a formal collar, looking thoughtfully to the side. The overall appearance of the planetary body is somewhat hazy and distant.

The video segment presents a sepia-toned image with the text "Percival Lowell in 1914" displayed in the top left corner. It shows a man, presumably Percival Lowell, dressed in a dark suit and a cap, seated on a small wooden platform that is part of a multi-level wooden ladder. The man is holding a rope or cord with his right hand, which he uses to elevate himself and the platform. As he ascends, a large, dark-colored telescope comes into view, and by the end of the clip, he is looking through its eyepiece, with his left hand resting on his lap. The setting appears to be an observatory, with a background of light-colored wooden paneling.

The video opens with a sepia-toned image from 1914 showing astronomer Percival Lowell looking through a large, classic telescope within an observatory. This transitions to another sepia-toned photo of American astronomer Clyde Tombaugh wearing glasses, a suit, and a tie, peering through a smaller, personal telescope. Following this, a document titled "Orbital Elements" is displayed, comparing predicted orbital characteristics by Lowell with actual observations of Pluto, showing columns for "Lowell" and "Pluto" with rows for "Mean Distance (AU*)", "Eccentricity", "Inclination", "Perihelion date*", "Period (years)", and "Mass (Earth=1)". The video then shows a screenshot of an "Ask an Astronomer" webpage, highlighting text that explains most planets rotate counter-clockwise, but Uranus rotates "on its side" due to a large planetoid hit, and Venus rotates backwards. Next, a grayscale image labeled "Jan. 24, 1986. Voyager 2" shows a bright, blurry disc of Uranus with faint rings, then another grayscale image reveals faint, concentric rings around a dark center, with small, bright moons labeled "1986U8" and "1986U7" within the ring system. This is followed by a split-screen graphic from "ESA/Hubble" depicting a light blue Uranus with its rings seen edge-on, with labels indicating "Outer Rings," "Inner Rings," "Uranus," and the "Ring Plane." A "NASA" diagram then illustrates Uranus with its full ring system and numerous moons (including Cordelia, Ophelia, Bianca, Cressida, Desdemona, Juliet, Portia, Rosalind, Belinda, Perdita, Puck, Miranda, and "New moons, 'Mab'" and "'Cupid'") orbiting within and around the rings, highlighting "Two new outer rings" (R1 and U2). The segment concludes with a close-up grayscale image from "NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute" showing two distinct, bright rings of Uranus with two small, bright moons, one positioned inside and one outside the main rings, appearing to "shepherd" them.

The video displays a monochrome, cosmic scene featuring a luminous, arched planetary ring system against a dark background, likely from Saturn. At the top left of the frame, white text reads "NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute," identifying the image source. In the upper right corner, a small, static, cartoon-like icon of a person with a mustache and a hat (possibly a cowboy hat) holding a staff is visible. Initially, a bright, spherical object, presumably a moon, is seen in the upper left. As the video progresses, another smaller, bright, spherical object travels along the inner edge of the glowing ring. This smaller moon gravitationally interacts with the ring material, causing noticeable wave-like disturbances and subtle shifts in the ring's structure, pulling and shaping the ring particles as it moves. The scene remains constant in its black and white aesthetic and overall composition, with the primary dynamic element being the moon's movement and its effect on the rings.

The video segment displays a simulated solar system with a vibrant purple, glowing sphere at its center, representing a star. Several spherical celestial bodies of varying sizes and colors, including black, brown, striped, and light blue planets (some with rings), orbit the central sphere along distinct dotted white paths. The background is a dark blue grid, giving the impression of a cosmic environment. In the top right corner, a small, translucent, static image of a man's head and shoulders, appearing to be a historical figure, is visible. Throughout the short clip, the celestial bodies continuously move along their orbital trajectories, and the overall perspective subtly rotates, creating a dynamic visualization of planetary motion.

The video segment opens with an animated scene depicting a large, fiery, volcanic-looking planet occupying the upper half of the frame, its surface appearing molten and glowing intensely orange and red. Below it, a bright white light illuminates a landscape of orange and red clouds, with several luminous streaks, resembling meteors or rockets, flying towards the light from the right. Text in the top left corner reads "Igor Zh / Shutterstock" and a small circular icon of a man's head is visible in the top right. The scene then transitions to a black and white image of a celestial body, possibly a moon or planet, encircled by a ring labeled "ε ring". Several smaller dots around it are labeled "Puck", "Belinda", "Portia", and "Miranda", with a faint "star" indicated in the top right, alongside the same small icon of a man's head. This is followed by a vibrant cosmic scene featuring a large, dark blue planet (implied to be Neptune by the narration) set against a backdrop of a colorful galaxy with swirling pink and white nebulae and stars, with the man's head icon remaining in the top right. Finally, the video transitions to a close-up shot of a large, intricately carved stone wall covered in ancient script, with "Trilingual cuneiform inscription of Xerxes" displayed in the top left. The script is etched into a light brown, rocky surface, divided into vertical columns, with some green foliage visible at the bottom of the structure.

The video segment begins with a static shot showcasing multiple small, dark, metallic figurines, identified by the overlay text as "ancient Mesopotamian gods, wearing characteristic horned crowns." These stylized human-like figures are displayed on clear acrylic stands against a blurred, muted background suggesting a museum setting. Each figurine is adorned with an elaborate, often multi-tiered or twisted horned crown, and some are depicted in seated or embracing postures with elongated objects. At 0:15, the scene abruptly cuts to an aerial view of a vast, arid, light brown landscape, with the text overlay "Band of holes in Peru." The terrain features undulating hills or ridges, upon which numerous small, dark, circular depressions are meticulously arranged in long, parallel bands, creating a striking pattern across the dry earth.

The video opens with an aerial shot of a dry, hilly landscape in Peru, displaying a long, winding band of numerous small, circular holes stretching across the uneven terrain, identified by the on-screen text "Band of holes in Peru." The scene transitions to a split view, showing three different aerial perspectives of these holes: a closer, grid-like arrangement in the top-left, a wider view of the winding band in the bottom-left, and a grayscale image of the holes traversing the landscape on the right. Subsequently, the video shifts to an aerial view of a flat, sandy desert near a road, revealing three large geoglyphs: a tree-like figure labeled "70m," a pair of hands or paws labeled "50m," and two parallel lines labeled "188m." The final shot is a close-up of an ancient relief carving or fresco depicting two bearded figures in ornate attire, standing on either side of a stylized "Tree of Life" or sacred tree, with a winged disc symbol above it, while two smaller figures are partially visible behind them.
